masthead.purpose: The uppercase wordmark, 900, in the 7rem red band (--text-xl on a phone).

headline.purpose: The champion's name, 900 at up to 6rem under a 6px ink rule, beside a 優勝 stamp stretched to its height; the one headline on the page.

title.purpose: The tournament name in the deck line (--text-lg 800).

name-maegashira.purpose: Foot of the name ladder; also Juryo and the lower divisions.

name-jp.purpose: Ring names and rank kanji in mincho.

label.purpose: Condensed caps for toggles, picker, stamps and the status badge at --text-sm 800; tab names, section-bar labels and side-box heads step up to --text-lg 900.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Print is flat; nothing in the page flow casts a shadow.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Float: the scroll-to-top button and the skip link. Night: 0 4px 14px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5).

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: The wrestler and stable dialogs. Night: 0 18px 48px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7), 0 3px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4).

shadows.name: highlighter-edges
shadows.purpose: Not depth: extends the highlighter screen past a name without changing its measure.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Hover tints, colour changes on controls.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Language slider, sheet fade on tab switch, search focus ring.

motion.name: fadeIn
motion.purpose: Header entrance, sheet arrival, dialog backdrop.

motion.name: riseIn
motion.value: @keyframes translateY(4px) → 0, 200ms, 25ms stagger on the first ten rows
motion.purpose: Rows, once per page load (gated by data-entered on <main>).

motion.name: modalSlideUp
motion.purpose: Dialog entrance. Budget: four effects, three in use, none loop.

components.name: Masthead Band

components.name: Basho Picker

narrative.overview:
The banzuke as the results page of a Japanese sports daily on the morning after a day of the basho: newsprint grey under a white sheet, a kin-aka red masthead band closed by an ink rule, black section bars where the rank tier changes, condensed heavy names that scale with rank, the ○● record set as a 星取表 in fixed day columns grouped by five, and a yellow highlighter screened over the thing that matters now: the champion's name, the yusho race while it is open, the name you searched for.

It is a working table first. The world lends four things only: type (Sofia Sans Condensed with a newspaper's appetite for weight, Noto Serif JP mincho for Japanese names and rank kanji as a paper sets names in its body text), palette (newsprint, ink, kin-aka, highlighter), density (a sports table's tight, aligned rhythm on a 4px base), and one signature move: **the highlighter**, 網掛け, the yellow screen a sports desk lays over the leader's line.

**What this deliberately avoids:** the cream-paper-and-vermilion-seal look this site used to wear (and that every "Japanese" interface defaults to); dark stats dashboards with neon; gold; rounded cards, pills and soft shadows; small tracked caps under 12px; rank told by hue alone; decorative Japanese motifs. No Rising Sun forms, ever: the masthead is a flat band, never rays.

The wrestler and stable dialogs are set as a player file (選手名鑑) on the same sheet: see Dialogs under Components.
keyCharacteristics: A full-bleed red band closed by a 6px masthead rule (4px on phones), then everything on newsprint.
One white sheet opened by a 5px ink rule that the division tabs stand on.
Rank carried by type size (about 2.6x from Yokozuna to Maegashira on desktop), with red reserved for sanyaku kanji and the Yokozuna's solid rail block.
Square everything: radius 0, 1.5px ink borders on controls, 1px hairlines between rows.
Flat print: only what floats over the page (dialogs, the scroll button) casts a shadow.
Three keyframe effects, entrance once per page load, nothing loops.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Red ranks, black selects, yellow highlights. A colour never borrows another's job.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Yellow only ever sits under text, and only on what the reader is looking for or what matters now. If two things on screen are highlighted, one of them is wrong: the yusho race drops its screen once the champion is decided, and while searching the champion's screen yields to the matches.

rules.name: The Fill-Is-Band Rule
rules.body: Red as a ground is `--band` with `--on-band`; red as a letterform is `--accent`. Never fill with `--accent`.

rules.name: The Ladder Rule
rules.body: Rank is told by name size and weight first, red second, never by hue alone.

rules.name: The 12px Floor
rules.body: Nothing a reader taps or needs is set below `--text-xs` (12px); condensed caps labels sit at `--text-sm` (13px) and get their legibility from weight, not tracking.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the document flow casts a shadow. `box-shadow` inside the sheet is only ever a drawing tool: the highlighter's edges, a kadoban outline, a focus ring.

rules.name: The Tier Change Rule
rules.body: A section bar marks where the tier changes inside a sheet. The first tier of any sheet is headed by the selected tab directly above it (and the sanyaku by the rail's own stamps), so no division draws a bar under its own tab; in Makuuchi only 前頭 gets one. Every tier keeps its `<h2>` for structure, visually hidden where no bar is drawn.

dos: **Do** keep red for rank and stamps, black for selection, yellow for the highlighter (The Three Inks Rule).
**Do** set names in Sofia Sans Condensed at ladder sizes and Japanese names and rank kanji in Noto Serif JP 700.
**Do** draw controls square: 1.5px ink border, sheet face, ink fill when selected.
**Do** draw the highlighter with a background plus two hard `box-shadow` edges, so highlighting never changes layout.
**Do** keep every control ≥44px tall on a phone and every label ≥12px.
**Do** keep the List free of sideways scroll from 360px; shrink marks with `cqi` before letting anything overflow.
donts: **Don't** round a corner, add a gradient, or cast a shadow from anything in the page flow.
**Don't** highlight two things on one screen.
**Don't** use cream, gold, or a decorative seal; a red stamp always states a fact (優勝, promotion, the wordmark's 番付).
**Don't** add a fifth keyframe effect (four budgeted, three in use: `fadeIn`, `riseIn`, `modalSlideUp`) or anything that loops.
**Don't** draw Rising Sun rays or other decorative Japanese motifs.
